title.narrative: SPVO – Harnessing Avocado Resources for Value Enhancement and Sustainability Transformation (HARVEST)

description.narrative: The HARVEST project aims to address social and interlinked environmental challenges in Rwanda’s avocado value chain, improving the livelihoods of smallholder farmers while promoting sustainable practices in the sector. This is done by building a more inclusive, responsible and commercially viable avocado value chain in Rwanda. During the local impact assessment in Phase A, it was found that many smallholder farmers own only a few avocado trees and face low and unstable incomes, fragmented market access, non-transparent pricing, poor harvesting and post-harvest practices, declining soil fertility, and limited access to affordable inputs and extension services. The assessment also identified gaps in traceability, certification readiness, occupational safety, formal labor practices and grievance mechanisms across parts of the value chain.During Phase B, the project will work with 8,000 smallholder farmers, prioritizing women and youth, through Regional and satellite avocado hubs in Gisagara District . The hubs will provide local access to training, aggregation, sorting, weighing, storage, inputs and market linkages. Farmers will receive practical support on avocado tree management, climate-smart agronomy, safe harvesting, post-harvest handling, record-keeping and traceability. A pilot group of farmers will be supported towards Rainforest Alliance certification and access to premium markets.The project will improve farmers’ access to organic fertiliser through the hub network, supported by practical training and field demonstrations. By complementing existing fertiliser practices, this is expected to improve soil health, nutrient management and crop performance, contributing to a targeted 10% increase in yields and a 5–10% increase in net farmer income. The hub network will also support more transparent aggregation, better traceability and stronger market linkages, while creating an estimated new jobs. At the same time, the project will strengthen occupational health and safety, worker feedback and grievance systems, and aggregators and suppliers will be supported to apply clearer labor and sourcing standards. The consortium partners will integrate responsible business conduct, due diligence and monitoring into their operations, helping to establish a safer, fairer and more accountable avocado value chain that can continue beyond the project period.
